pronunciation.title: Say it right from day one

rules.explain: a=AH, e=EH, i=EE, o=OH, u=OO. Always. So CASA is KAH-sah.

examples.en: house
table

rules.rule: H is silent, J sounds like H
rules.explain: HOLA is OH-lah (no H sound). J in JUEVES sounds like English H: HWEH-vehs.

examples.en: hello
Thursday

rules.explain: Ñ is like NY in canyon: NIÑO = NEEN-yoh. LL and Y sound like Y in yes.

examples.en: boy
street

rules.explain: Tap your tongue once for R. PERRO (dog) rolls longer than PERO (but).

examples.en: but
dog

rules.explain: Most words stress the middle: HOLA = OH-lah, GRACIAS = GRAH-syahs. An accent mark (á) forces stress there.

examples.en: thanks
coffee

alphabet.title: The Haitian Creole alphabet: 26 letters, three nasal vowels
alphabet.explain: Haitian Creole (Kreyòl) writes in the Latin alphabet with a few spelling habits of its own: the apostrophe (wouf) is a real sound, and an n before a vowel marks nasal vowels (an, en, on, in, ou).

counting.title: Counting in Haitian Creole: 0 to 15
counting.explain: Eleven and up are their own words: onz (11), douz (12), trèz (13), katòz (14), kinz (15) — once you know them, the pattern above does the rest.
rules: Nasal vowels: an, en, in, on, ou — the air leaves through the nose.
Stress almost always falls on the last syllable.
The w is pronounced like the English h in hmm — a stop in the throat.
